evals.prompt: Set up a brand-new monorepo for our project 'acme-platform' so Claude Code and other agents can navigate it. It'll hold a frontend, a backend, and some workers.
evals.expected_output: A scaffolded repository with AGENTS.md, a minimal docs/index.md handoff, docs/component-guide.md, a components/ central folder, and validation templates. AGENTS.md and docs/index.md contain generated markers for easy-docs, the response recommends running easy-docs for the docs system, and the scaffold prints a stable JSON summary of what it created.
assertions: A root AGENTS.md file is created
docs/index.md is created with BEGIN GENERATED DOCS INDEX markers
A components/ central folder is created (monorepo target)
AGENTS.md links to docs/index.md and docs/component-guide.md
AGENTS.md contains BEGIN GENERATED CORE DOCS markers
The response recommends running easy-docs for the docs system
The scaffold helper prints a JSON summary of created files/directories
The monorepo entrypoint section is named 'Component Entrypoints'

evals.prompt: We need a sites repo for ollem.io, and there's also a mobile version of the site. Scaffold it for us.
evals.expected_output: Because a sites project has a mobile variant, the agent asks one concise question about the preferred naming pattern (e.g. m-ollem-io vs ollem-io.mobile) before creating folders, then scaffolds a sites/ layout using the normalized domain folder name ollem-io.
assertions: The agent asks one concise question about the mobile naming pattern before creating folders
It offers concrete options such as 'm-ollem-io' or 'ollem-io.mobile'
After a choice is made, a sites/ollem-io folder is created (domain normalized with hyphens)
AGENTS.md uses the 'Site Entrypoints' section name for the sites target

evals.prompt: Here's our existing Node service repo — it has a package.json but no AGENTS.md and no docs/. Adopt it into the agent-friendly structure.
evals.expected_output: For an adopt target the agent does NOT immediately restructure files. It maps the current repo, classifies package.json as an entrypoint marker, reports the structural gaps (missing AGENTS.md, project.md, docs/index.md), notes that the docs system itself is delegated to the easy-docs skill, and explains what must change before applying any migration.
assertions: The output is an adoption/migration plan, not an immediate bulk restructuring of files
It identifies the missing AGENTS.md and missing docs/index.md
It identifies the missing project.md
It classifies package.json as an entrypoint marker file
It notes the docs system (headers, indexes, standards docs) is delegated to the easy-docs skill
It does not delete or move existing files without first explaining the change

evals.prompt: Bootstrap this empty repo with a custom layout: all deployable code should live under an apps/ folder.
evals.expected_output: A scaffolded repository using the custom target with apps/ as the central folder. The pre-commit hook pattern watches apps/ alongside docs/ and scripts/, and AGENTS.md uses the 'Target Entrypoints' section name.
assertions: An apps/ central folder is created
AGENTS.md uses the 'Target Entrypoints' section name for the custom target
prek.toml's fast-quality-gates hook file pattern covers apps/ (not only docs/ and scripts/)
A root readme.md and .gitignore are created

evals.prompt: Run the repository bootstrap again on this repo. It was already scaffolded as a site target and we customized AGENTS.md afterwards — make sure nothing gets clobbered.
evals.expected_output: The scaffold helper is re-run idempotently: customized files such as AGENTS.md are left untouched, the JSON summary reports them under 'existing', and no destructive overwrite happens.
assertions: The customized AGENTS.md content is preserved byte-for-byte
The JSON summary lists already-present files under 'existing' rather than 'created'
No existing file is overwritten or deleted
